title: dependency-supply-chain-authz-evidence-playbook-2026
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook defines controls, evidence requirements, and operational procedures for authorization, audit logging, retention and incident handling of the software dependency supply chain across Redwood Inference build and release pipelines. It is intended for engineering managers, security engineers, SRE, and compliance auditors.

Goals

- Ensure reproducible provenance for all third-party and internal build artifacts.
- Define minimum evidence packages required for regulatory audits and internal investigations.
- Provide a fast runbook for suspected supply-chain compromise, including containment and rollback.
- Integrate controls with Secure SDLC gates and CI/CD authorization policy enforcement.

Scope

This document covers dependencies and artifacts ingested or produced by:
- Build CI (internal Jenkins/GitHub Actions runners)
- Artifact registries (container registry, private PyPI/NPM proxies, model artifact stores)
- Release orchestration (canary/blue-green deployments)
- Developer-local package management where artifacts are published to production paths

Out of scope: upstream vendor contractual terms (see procurement), runtime-only telemetry unrelated to artifact provenance.

Roles & Ownership

- Security (owner): maintain this playbook, review evidence packages during audits, run compromise simulations.
- Eng Platform (owner of CI/IaC): implement and operate CI authz hooks, artifact signing integration, and secure storage for evidence.
- Release Engineering: enforce release gates that require evidence bundles before promotion.
- SRE / Incident Response: execute forensic runbooks and coordinate with Security for escalations.

Required Controls (high-level)

1) Artifact provenance enforcement
- All build artifacts must be signed using the company KMS-backed signing service (artifact-sign-service).
- Signatures must include: pipeline-id, git-sha, builder-id, and deterministic build flags.

2) CI Authorization (authz)
- CI jobs that publish artifacts require short-lived deployment tokens issued by the CI-authZ service with scopes: publish:artifact, promote:release.
- Least-privilege: tokens are scoped to repository/branch and expire within 1 hour.

3) Immutable audit logging
- Publish events for the following to the audit stream (immutable store): build.start, build.finish, artifact.signed, artifact.published, token.issued, token.revoked, release.promoted, release.rollback.
- Logs must include correlation_id and be indexed with at most 5 minutes lag.

Evidence Package Requirements

Each release or artifact promoted to production must be accompanied by an evidence package. Minimum required items: 
- artifact-manifest.json (signed): fields [artifact_id, digest, builder, build_time, git_sha, build_pipeline_id]
- signature.pem: artifact signature produced by artifact-sign-service
- ci-run-log.tgz: compressed CI job logs for the build (stdout/stderr + exit codes)
- dependency-lockfile (e.g., requirements.txt.lock / package-lock.json) with resolved digests
- vulnerability-scan-report.json (if available)
- promotion-record.json: who promoted, when, target clusters/regions

Evidence Retention Matrix (summary table)

| Artifact type | Minimum retention | Primary store | Evidence owner |
|--------------|-------------------|---------------|----------------|
| Container images | 2 years | private-registry-backed storage | Eng Platform |
| Python/Rust/JS packages published internally | 2 years | internal artifact proxy | Eng Platform |
| Model artifacts (production) | 5 years (regulatory) | model-store + cold archive | Product/ML Platform |
| CI logs for release builds | 1 year | encrypted log-archive | Eng Platform |
| Audit-log events (immutable) | 7 years | audit-immutable-store | Security |
\n(Notes: extended retention for models is required by some customers and by internal policy.)

Searchability & SLA for Audit Evidence

- Security must be able to retrieve any evidence package for a given artifact_id within 2 business hours (target).
- Indexed audit logs: 99% of critical events searchable within 1 hour of occurrence. Maximum allowed lag: 4 hours.

CI/CD Integration Examples

1) Example policy check (pseudo YAML) for enforcing evidence before promotion:

---
when: promotion.requested
checks:
  - evidence: artifact-manifest.json exists and signature.pem validates against KMS key: "projects/redwood/keys/artifact-signing"
  - ci_logs: artifact build job logs available and non-empty
  - vulnerabilities: scan_status != "blocker"
actions:
  - if all pass: allow_promote
  - else: block_promote and notify(team:release-engineering)
---

2) Example artifact-manifest.json (single-line preview)

{"artifact_id":"image.redwood/v1/backend:2026-02-20-abcdef","digest":"sha256:...","git_sha":"abcdef123","builder":"ci-runner-15","build_pipeline_id":"ci-3245"}

Forensic Runbook: Suspected Compromised Dependency

Trigger: a vendor advisory, anomalous runtime behavior, or detection from supply-chain scanner indicating a dependency compromise.

Immediate actions (T+0 to T+2 hours)
1) Triage & containment
  - Create incident in PagerDuty channel: "supply-chain-compromise" and assign Security and Release Eng on-call.
  - Block new promotions: flip CI gate flag (release.gate.block=true).
  - Revoke active CI publish tokens issued in previous 72 hours: CI-authZ -> revoke scope publish:artifact.

2) Evidence collection (must be immutable)
  - Snapshot relevant artifact manifests and signatures for impacted artifacts.
  - Pull associated CI logs and compress as evidence bundle.
  - Export audit-log slice (time-range -72h..now) for events: artifact.published, token.issued, token.revoked, user.authn.
  - Record chain of transitive dependencies from lockfiles.

3) Impact assessment (T+2 to T+12 hours)
  - Map deployed clusters/regions using promotion-record.json for artifacts with the impacted dependency.
  - Identify customers or environments with heightened residency constraints.
  - Decide rollback vs patch: prioritize rollback for critical signed images; patch for mitigations that do not require full rollback.

4) Remediation & verification (T+12 to T+72 hours)
  - Create and sign a fixed artifact using a trusted builder retreaced to a known-good git commit.
  - Run regression and fuzz tests defined in pre-approved evaluation sets.
  - Update promotion control center and allow promotions only after Security sign-off.

Evidence Packaging & Audit Handover

- Evidence bundles must be hashed and stored in the immutable evidence bucket with ACLs limited to Security and Legal.
- Handover to Legal for any regulatory/customer notification must include a manifest of evidence object IDs and a short executive summary (500–800 words) describing root cause, timeline, and impact.

Exception & Risk Acceptance Process

When a required control cannot be implemented immediately (e.g., third-party tooling that does not support signing), follow the temporary exception process: 
1) Request exception via the exception portal (link in internal tools) with fields: control_id, justification, compensating_controls, expiry_date (max 90 days).
2) Security reviews and assigns risk score; if score > 70 (high), refer to CISO for approval.
3) If approved, define compensating controls and evidence expected during the exception window (e.g., increased log sampling, daily manual artifact scans).
4) Track exceptions in the risk register and schedule mandatory remediation before expiry.

Metrics & Continuous Improvement

- Monthly: sampling of 10 production promotions to verify evidence completeness (artifact manifests, signatures, CI logs).
- Quarterly: table-top supply-chain compromise drill involving Security, Release Eng, Legal, and Product.
- KPIs: percent of production promotions with complete evidence (target 100%), mean time to evidence retrieval (target < 2 hours).

Appendix A: CLI snippets for evidence retrieval

# Retrieve artifact manifest and signature for artifact_id
redwood-cli artifacts fetch --id image.redwood/v1/backend:2026-02-20-abcdef --output evidence-bundle/

# Export audit-log slice (example)
audit-export --start 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z --end 2026-03-10T00:00:00Z --filter "resource:artifact AND event:published" --dest evidence-bundle/audit-slice.ndjson

Appendix B: Example minimal CI step to sign artifact (GitHub Actions snippet)

- name: Sign artifact
  run: |
    export ARTIFACT_ID=${{ env.IMAGE }}\n    artifact-sign --artifact $ARTIFACT_ID --kms-key projects/redwood/keys/artifact-signing --out signature.pem
  env: 
    KMS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.KMS_SIGN_TOKEN }}
